criteria.statement: Get, GetInt, GetBool and GetDuration all call one unexported method lookup(section, key string) (string, error), and none of them reads c.sections directly
The exported API, every returned value and every error message of the four getters are exactly as before the refactor

criteria.baseline: it must pass on the input snapshot, as a regression guard; interlock saw it pass there (run run-da48d758a2f04aa0)

goal:
`getters.go` repeats the same section-and-key lookup in `Get`, `GetInt`, `GetBool` and `GetDuration`. Move it into one unexported method,

```go
func (c *Config) lookup(section, key string) (string, error)
```

and make all four getters use it, so that none of them reads `c.sections` directly any more.

This is a pure refactor. The exported API, every returned value and every error message must stay exactly as they are now. The tests run with `go test ./...`.

previous_result.summary:
I added `lookup(section, key)` to `getters.go`, and `Get`, `GetInt`, `GetBool` and `GetDuration` now all call it. Only `lookup` reads `c.sections`. `go test ./...` passes on the final tree, and the interlock regression check passed too.

`GetBool` words its missing-key error differently from the other three ("key %q not set" instead of "no key %q"). To keep every message identical, `lookup` returns a small `missingKeyError` type, and `GetBool` recognises it and rewrites the message.

I added `TestGetterErrorMessages` to `getters_test.go`. It pins the missing-section and missing-key messages of all four getters, including the top-level cases. I recorded claims for all three criteria: regression and behaviour at `tested`, structure at `static`. The structure and behaviour criteria still need an independent check.
